title: Only 8% Pass This Paramedic Entrance Exam
summary: Explore Dispatch Briefing, Body & Signals, Scene & Communication, Decisions Under Pressure, Final Response across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: Dispatch Briefing, Body & Signals, Scene & Communication, Decisions Under Pressure, Final Response. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited paramedic entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Emergency procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local guidance and appropriately qualified emergency professionals.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

paramedic-r1q1.question: Which organ pumps blood around the body?

answers.a2: Lungs

visual.ariaLabel: Call logged at 14:35 and arrival at 15:12

paramedic-r3q2.question: A call is logged at 14:35. The crew reaches the destination at 15:12. How much time has passed?

answers.a2: 47 minutes

visual.ariaLabel: Used sharp, broken glass and a clear exit

paramedic-r4q3.question: How should the floor hazard be handled first?

answers.a1: Isolate the hazard and report it
answers.a2: Move it carefully with a gloved hand
answers.a3: Slide it away from the walkway with your shoe
answers.a4: Leave it until the scene is quieter

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse unchanged, breathing increased, alertness unchanged, skin warmth unchanged

answers.a2: Alertness

paramedic-r1q5.question: Which opening makes the clearest handover?

answers.a2: Here are all the minor details in random order
answers.a3: At 14:20, breathing became faster and alertness decreased
answers.a4: I already know exactly what caused it

paramedic-r1q6.context: A routine equipment checklist is due soon. At the same time, a person who was comfortable becomes pale, dizzy and less responsive.
paramedic-r1q6.question: Which takes priority?

answers.a1: Prioritise the person’s sudden deterioration and seek qualified help
answers.a2: Complete the routine checklist before responding
answers.a3: Wait until the checklist deadline has passed
answers.a4: Choose whichever task is physically nearest

visual.ariaLabel: Oxygen-rich blood travels from the lungs through an unknown chamber before the left ventricle

paramedic-r2q1.question: Which chamber receives oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs?

answers.a2: Right atrium

paramedic-r2q3.question: Which body system carries signals between the brain and the rest of the body?

answers.a2: Skeletal system

paramedic-r2q4.question: Which statement best describes the kidneys?

answers.a1: They exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide
answers.a2: They remove wastes from blood and help regulate water balance

paramedic-r2q5.context: Earlier, both hand grips were equal. Now the right grip is unchanged, but the left grip is weaker than before.
paramedic-r2q5.question: Which body-function detail changed?

answers.a2: Both grips strengthened

paramedic-r5q3.context: Earlier the person was alert and answered promptly. Now they are drowsy and respond much more slowly.
paramedic-r5q3.question: Which newly recorded change matters most?

answers.a2: The time written on the card

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse 80 then 92 then 108, with pallor and dizziness

paramedic-r5q4.question: What is the best interpretation of this pattern?

answers.a2: The combined trend suggests deterioration needing prompt qualified assessment
answers.a4: The symptoms can be ignored because no diagnosis is shown

paramedic-r1q4.question: A live electrical cable lies across the only doorway. What comes first?

answers.a2: Keep everyone clear and get qualified help to make it safe
answers.a3: Move it with a dry object
answers.a4: Ask a bystander to watch it

paramedic-r4q1.question: A person is beside moving traffic with no protected working area. What is safest?

answers.a1: Keep clear, identify the danger and seek appropriate scene support
answers.a2: Walk into traffic and wave vehicles around
answers.a3: Ask the person to cross the road immediately
answers.a4: Place equipment in the road to slow vehicles

paramedic-r4q4.question: A task may expose the face and hands to splashing body fluid. What guides PPE choice?

answers.a1: The colour of the equipment bag
answers.a2: Whether the person looks unwell
answers.a4: The assessed exposure risk, including hand and eye or face protection

paramedic-r6q5.question: A coughing person is sharing a small waiting area. Which general safety action fits the visible risk?

answers.a2: Turn off all ventilation without assessment
answers.a3: Encourage respiratory and hand hygiene and follow risk-based precautions

visual.ariaLabel: Vehicle stopped, two people, strong fuel smell

paramedic-r9q4.question: Which detail is most urgent to hand over?

answers.a2: The number of windows
answers.a3: The fuel smell and possible ignition hazard

paramedic-r6q2.question: A person keeps nodding but has not understood. What should happen next?

answers.a1: Repeat the same explanation more slowly
answers.a2: Ask, ‘Do you understand?’ and continue if they say yes
answers.a3: Shorten the explanation but keep the same terminology
answers.a4: Use plain words and check back

paramedic-r6q1.question: A person says, “I'm terrified.” Which response is best?

answers.a1: There is nothing to be scared about
answers.a2: Try not to think about it
answers.a3: I guarantee everything will be fine
answers.a4: I can see this is frightening. Tell me what worries you most

paramedic-r10q5.context: The person says, “I do not want this discussed where others can hear, and I still do not understand why you are asking.”
paramedic-r10q5.question: Which response protects privacy and checks understanding?

answers.a1: Continue the discussion where everyone can hear
answers.a2: Avoid explaining and ask the same questions again
answers.a3: Move to an appropriate private setting, explain plainly and check understanding
answers.a4: Ask a bystander to explain on your behalf

paramedic-r2q6.context: The person's chest is moving, but very little air movement can be detected and they cannot speak normally.
paramedic-r2q6.question: Which concern has the highest priority?

answers.a2: A possible airway or breathing problem needing immediate qualified assessment

paramedic-r5q6.context: Person A feels well and their observations remain steady. Person B is newly clammy and dizzy, and their pulse has risen across three checks.
paramedic-r5q6.question: Who needs attention first?

answers.a1: Person B, because several changes point to deterioration
answers.a2: Person A, because their observations were recorded first
answers.a3: Both can wait because neither has a named diagnosis
answers.a4: Person A, because their observations are currently stable

paramedic-r7q1.context: The scene was initially reported as safe. A second update says smoke is now entering the room and the nearest exit is becoming difficult to use.
paramedic-r7q1.question: Which new information should change the response most?

answers.a1: The original report that the scene was safe
answers.a2: The developing smoke and threatened exit route
answers.a3: The time the first report was written
answers.a4: The number of words in the update

visual.ariaLabel: 0.3 litres plus 450 millilitres plus 250 millilitres equals what total

paramedic-r3q3.question: What is the combined recorded volume in millilitres?

answers.a2: 950 mL

items: PERSON A::Sore wrist · normal speech · steady observations
PERSON B::Collapsed · pale · rapid breathing · new confusion
visual.ariaLabel: Person A has a sore wrist, normal speech and steady observations. Person B collapsed and is pale, breathing rapidly and newly confused.

paramedic-r10q6.question: Which person should receive priority attention?

answers.a2: Equal priority

items: SHALLOW BREATHING → LESS GAS EXCHANGE → ? → LESS OXYGEN TO TISSUES
visual.ariaLabel: Shallow breathing, less gas exchange, unknown, less oxygen to tissues

paramedic-r10q1.question: If shallow breathing reduces gas exchange, what downstream effect follows most directly?

answers.a2: Less oxygen enters the blood

visual.ariaLabel: Breathing 16 alert, then 22 anxious, then 28 drowsy

paramedic-r10q2.question: What is the best interpretation of the complete trend?

answers.a2: Only the middle check matters
answers.a3: The values can be ignored because no diagnosis is named
answers.a4: Breathing is worsening while responsiveness is declining

paramedic-r8q2.question: A 1.2 L total is divided equally across four recorded periods. How much belongs to each period?

answers.a2: 300 mL

paramedic-r10q4.context: INCIDENT RECORD — An aggressive person is throwing objects near the entrance. Equipment partly blocks the nearest exit route.
paramedic-r10q4.question: What is the safest response to the combined hazards?

answers.a1: Keep clear, move others towards a safer route and alert appropriate help
answers.a2: Approach and argue until the person stops
answers.a3: Retrieve the equipment beside the person before leaving
answers.a4: Ask an untrained bystander to block the thrown objects
